_comment: Experiment results and provenance. Figures and tables are not currently generated from this file. Each entry records the machine state it was measured under; numbers from different states must never be combined into a ratio.

platform.bw_method: saturating OpenMP reduction, not vendor spec

ab_interleaved._comment: FINAL 2026-10-05, scripts/pp_baseline.sh. Two interleaved rounds of -r 5 per cell, variant chosen via LD_LIBRARY_PATH over immutable snapshots. Supersedes ALL earlier prefill numbers, including every measurement taken with the cp-over-mapped-.so method, which segfaulted running processes and produced spurious variance. Headline uses t=16 for consistency with the profiling run (74.60) from which the Amdahl bound is derived.
ab_interleaved.method: pp512, -r 5, two interleaved rounds, LD_LIBRARY_PATH variant selection
ab_interleaved.headline: 3.47x at t=16 (21.17 -> 73.46); 3.28x at t=8
ab_interleaved.note: prefill variance is markedly higher at t=16 than t=8, consistent with SMT contention for per-core tile registers

prefill_profile._comment: perf record -F 999 -g on pp512, t=16. Shares are of total prefill runtime. The run this came from measured 74.60 tok/s, so the Amdahl bound MUST be derived from 512/74.60 s and no other wall time.

decode_profile._comment: perf on tg128. Kernel share corresponds to ~10 tok/s in isolation, i.e. 77% of roofline; the gap is synchronisation.

ladder._comment: Optimisation attribution. All six steps measured in ONE session on a loaded machine (pre-reboot). Internally comparable; NOT comparable to post-reboot absolutes. The paper must present these as a within-session series and never mix them with the clean-state numbers.

thread_scaling._comment: pp256/tg64, -r 2, single session. Note prefill variance at t=16 is large (see ab_interleaved); SMT destabilises prefill.

negative_results._comment: Interventions that did NOT recover the decode gap. All measured t=16 in one session.

plain_decode._comment: FINAL 2026-10-05, scripts/tg_baseline.sh. Variant selected via LD_LIBRARY_PATH over immutable snapshot dirs - NEVER by cp over a mapped .so, which corrupts running processes (error 14 segfaults) and invalidated our earlier campaign. Two interleaved rounds of -r 5 per cell. KEY RESULT: at t=16 both implementations saturate memory bandwidth and decode is invariant (ratio 0.99) despite a ~3x prefill spread. At t=8 the baseline has NOT saturated, so our kernel looks 25% better. Any decode comparison MUST state its thread count.
plain_decode.method: tg128, -r 5, two interleaved rounds, LD_LIBRARY_PATH variant selection
plain_decode.interpretation: decode is bandwidth-bound; at saturation a large prefill spread produces no decode spread. The baseline needs SMT to reach the ceiling (+27%); ours is already there at t=8 (+1.1%).
plain_decode.supports: the invariance claim, more strongly than the original +3% figure

speculative._comment: RE-MEASURED 2026-10-05 with scripts/mtp_bench.py against llama-server. This is the DEPLOYED configuration and belongs in the headline. Method: 3 fixed prompts x 2 trials = 6 requests per condition, n_predict=160, temperature=0, cache_prompt=false, t=16, c=8192, parallel=1. Identical prompts across conditions because acceptance is content-dependent. Kernel variant selected via LD_LIBRARY_PATH over snapshotted library sets - NEVER by cp over a mapped .so, which segfaults running processes. Decode tok/s is the server's own predicted_per_second.
speculative.acceptance_control: 50.9% vs 50.7% across kernels - near-identical, so the gain is compute, not better drafting. This is the cleanest control in the paper.
speculative.retracted_old_rows: Previous table (6.69/8.18/10.27/13.85) is superseded. The 13.85 'chat' row was 5 trials and must not be reported as a point estimate.

roofline._comment: 13.03 = 93.7/7.19. Note 7.19 GB = 6.70 GiB; the paper must state GiB vs GB explicitly because 93.7/6.70 would wrongly give 13.99.

precision_floor._comment: Withdrawn; the original comparison is not reproducible and is excluded from the released results.
